court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Shri. Vijay Jagdish Chheda vs Ms. Dimple Vijay Chheda
facts_of_case: Petitioner's marriage was solemnized with respondent on 15/10/1995. Respondent filed a petition seeking dissolution of marriage. Petitioner claims that respondent unilaterally redeemed mutual funds and deposited the amount in their joint account.

legal_principles.principle: The court fee provision applicable to a case must be fixed having regard to the substance and not the form of a plaint.
legal_principles.held: The Court has taken view that the Court fee provision applicable to a case must be fixed having regard to the substance and not the form of a plaint.
cited_cases: Bangalore Water Supply Board versus A. Rajappa and Ors, (1978) 2 SCC 213

legal_principles.principle: The relief sought in a case must be considered before levying court fee on the said document.
legal_principles.held: According to the learned counsel, what is important is to take into consideration the relief sought in a case, before levying court fee on the said document.
cited_cases: Bangalore Water Supply Board versus A. Rajappa and Ors, (1978) 2 SCC 213

legal_principles.principle: A claim seeking substantive relief capable of being valued in terms of monetary gain or prevention of monetary loss falls under Article 7 of Schedule I.
legal_principles.held: According to him, since the petitioner has sought re-transfer of the amount from the saving account of Axis Bank to the joint account of the petitioner and the respondent in HDFC Bank and he also sought a restraint order from utilizing the transferring or exhausting the amount, it is nothing short of a money suit.
cited_cases: Bangalore Water Supply Board versus A. Rajappa and Ors, (1978) 2 SCC 213

legal_principles.principle: A party seeking a relief which is not sought cannot be imported so as to charge court fee thereon.
legal_principles.held: The Court has taken view that the Court fee provision applicable to a case must be fixed having regard to the substance and not the form of a plaint.
cited_cases: Bangalore Water Supply Board versus A. Rajappa and Ors, (1978) 2 SCC 213

outcome.final_order: Direction was issued to the present petitioner to pay full ad-valorem court fees on the said amount.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo dat quod non habet
use_for_drafting: advising on court fees and procedures
